status: Core ledger, guarded orchestration, runtime fences and initial typed outcomes implemented with local fixture/crash tests. Original policy/store pinning, caller observation/recovery/settlement and workflow/Discord integration remain incomplete; no live continuation acceptance.
scope: Native VM runtime ownership transfer required by #1713 under #1703. Preserve healthy saved builder exports and provider aliases across a fenced controller handoff. This does not itself claim or finish an owner turn.

source_contracts.retention: #1746 preserves restored runtimes; retirement still owns final reclamation

glossary.workflow_lease: SQLite authority to dispatch or mutate a workflow; expiry never proves descendants stopped.
glossary.runtime_owner: A RuntimeOwner value contains workflow_id + lease_generation. When used as current authority in this amendment it always means effective_owner, never merely the creation value in owned.json.
glossary.audit_generation: Protected audit log/anchor namespace. A handoff seals the previous namespace and supplies a distinct healthy destination.
glossary.transfer: A durable old-owner/audit to new-owner/audit migration, preserving exact completed exports and aliases. It is not a native model turn, workflow retirement or shipment.
glossary.builder_inventory: Controller-observed provider/session IDs from protected workflow state. A provider alias resolves an ID to an owned runtime; neither a model response nor an audit UUID alone supplies this authority.
glossary.creation_owner: Immutable owner/audit provenance in owned.json at runtime creation. It is not overwritten on handoff.
glossary.effective_owner: Latest validated owner/audit in the native transfer ledger for this runtime, or its creation owner/audit when no transfer exists. Native resume, owner retirement and stale-scope cleanup use this one derived authority.
glossary.native_transfer_state: prepared holds immutable request, exclusive endpoint/runtime claims and growth reservation; completed atomically installs mappings/closures/receipt and releases claims/reservation; aborted atomically records superseding fenced retirement, has no completed receipt/mapping and releases claims/reservation. Both terminal records remain immutable history.
glossary.scope_retirement: Best-effort lifetime cleanup requested by NativeSession/Launch Drop, with captured owner/audit. It may mark an unchanged unclaimed runtime retired; it cannot supersede pending transfer or create an owner-closure intent.
glossary.fenced_retirement: Existing controller-authorized terminal or verified-audit-recovery retire_owned_runtimes operation. Only this authorization may close its exact owner and atomically abort an intersecting prepared transfer through D10.

decisions.decision: Add a Linux controller API that transfers all supplied source runtime owners to one newer owner of the same workflow and a distinct protected audit path. Require a current workflow lease in the caller immediately before the API and in the sealing callback. Source owners are an explicit immutable list; never infer them from a branch name or the last heartbeat.
decisions.why: A healthy runtime is currently either active-owned or retired. Retirement prevents resuming its saved native conversation.

decisions.decision: Use the existing native policy state root, StateLock and per-session kernel flock locks. Validate source/destination workflow identity, strictly increasing generation, absolute audit paths, private regular metadata, and exact registered builder inventory before changing any runtime owner. Bound the transfer to 64 source owners and 64 sessions; overflow is a named capacity refusal and never truncates inventory. Retired sessions are excluded from migration. Every non-retired source runtime must resolve to a supplied observed builder conversation; missing/uncertain observation, missing alias/export/completion, diagnostic or failed completion, foreign workflow, changed audit path and symlinks refuse. Empty inventory is valid only when no non-retired source runtime exists. A destination owner already closed in retired_owner refuses. Completion must be version 1, exit_code 0, diagnostic_only absent/false, launch_sha256 valid SHA-256, a single safe generation-* directory, worker_quiescence.remaining_workers == 0 and quiet_scans >= 2. Recursively hash the referenced export generation with no symlinks, regular owner-private files, <=64 MiB and <=4096 files; preserve exact alias and creation receipt bytes. Completion itself does not substitute for current kernel quiescence. The core scans all non-retired runtimes for the workflow and rejects any effective source owner/session omitted from the explicit request. Native session IDs are nonempty ASCII graphic strings of at most 256 bytes, matching Launch::observe_session; a longer workflow observation is ineligible rather than silently truncated. Every export generation root must be a same-UID directory with no group/other permission bits. Descendant directories must be same-UID, nonsymlink directories; legacy descendant mode bits are accepted only beneath that verified private root, which prevents other users from traversing the export. Regular files remain owner-private and single-link; all metadata stability checks remain mandatory. New producer exports create every directory component with mode 0700, independent of service umask. Never chmod or rewrite saved exports to make them eligible.
decisions.why: Keeping a session ID does not prove the export belongs to this workflow, and a completed controller process does not prove child quiescence. Legacy Python mkdir(parents=True) applied 0700 only to the final parent, so rejecting all legacy directory mode bits would strand otherwise private saved conversations. The private generation ancestor preserves the privacy boundary without modifying historical bytes.

decisions.decision: Lock order is native StateLock, then all affected session locks in lexical path order, then protected audit anchor locks. Session locks are nonblocking: busy means free deferral with no runtime metadata changes. Under these locks, run a controller callback that verifies and seals each source audit generation. Add healthy-handoff sealing to AuditLogger/AnchoredAudit: reject failed continuity, pending append or writer tickets; verify anchored bytes; verify every recorded required run-resource identity with run_resources::verify_quiescent; require every model admission to carry admission_schema_version 2 and the identical resource_identity JSON from exactly one preceding run_resource_admitted observation for the same provider; reject duplicate, missing, legacy-unbound or conflicting model-to-resource correlation; require prior controller generation less than destination generation. The seal is immutable and idempotent. Existing interrupted-audit recovery stays separate. The destination audit is a distinct private namespace and healthy before transfer starts. ProcessGroup::admit supplies the controller-read resource identity to AuditLogger at the same model charge/release boundary; legacy unprotected/non-deferred accounting retains its existing API and does not become eligible handoff proof. Protected writer ticket registration must acquire the same cross-process anchor lock as sealing, check that the generation is open, and create/fsync its ticket plus increment the local writer count before releasing that lock. Sealing excludes new registrations while checking outstanding tickets and publishing its seal. A late registration against a sealed generation refuses without creating a new ticket. Existing-seal replay is read-only: first verify the same handoff/request identity and anchored bytes, then return the identical stored proof without calling protected_health or appending. Rejected post-seal writes cannot invalidate a previously verified seal; real pre-seal continuity loss still prevents the initial seal. Add deterministic cross-process registration/sealing race and seal/late-write/crash/replay tests.
decisions.why: Kernel-empty resource removal revokes waiting supervisors, session locks protect exports, and sealing structurally rejects late audit writes. These are complementary controls.

decisions.decision: Use a versioned native-state transfer ledger in the same private FULL-synchronous SQLite database as retired_owner. The immutable request binds a controller-generated transfer UUID, workflow, sorted source effective owners/audit paths, destination owner/audit, exact observed provider/session/runtime mapping and creation-receipt/export/completion hashes. Reuse of a UUID with different inputs refuses. Prepare durably before sealing; after obtaining the immutable seal proofs, atomically commit old-owner closure, every effective-owner mapping and the completed receipt in one native SQLite transaction. A source owner already closed by terminal retirement or a different transfer refuses. Matching pending transfer replay revalidates the same inventory/proofs. The ledger is the authority for effective ownership; owned.json remains immutable creation provenance.
decisions.why: There is no reason to rewrite runtime files to transfer ownership. One native SQLite commit can move all effective owners together and retain original provenance; audit sealing remains a separately recoverable boundary.

decisions.decision: Do not replace owned.json or any export, completion or alias file. Add a resolver that verifies the immutable creation receipt hash and follows the native ledger to the latest effective owner/audit. The initial source is creation provenance; each completed transfer must extend the exact prior effective owner and strictly increase the generation within the same workflow. A malformed or disconnected chain refuses. Commit all source-to-destination mappings and old-owner closure atomically. A completed transfer replays its immutable receipt without reapplying old mappings, even if a later valid transfer has advanced a runtime again. No per-runtime staging files or rename cleanup protocol is introduced.
decisions.why: Immutable creation receipts plus one transactional effective-owner authority avoid half-renamed files, downgrade races and duplicate homes for current ownership.

decisions.decision: Old-owner closure fences subsequent native preparation through owner_retired. Resume resolves effective ownership and then validates that workflow/audit authority against the destination; successful completion, exact provider alias, non-retired runtime, guarded scope and current resource admission remain mandatory. Do not write retired.json or retired-owner.json for migrated sessions. Destination terminal retirement resolves effective ownership before marking sessions; replaying source retirement cannot mark a now-transferred runtime. Pruning retains its actual native predicate: validated retirement markers plus an available session flock. This amendment adds no process-reference checker. Transfer creates no retirement marker; destination/source retirement and delayed Drop must first resolve effective authority. Existing terminal reconciliation still owns kernel quiescence before authorizing retirement; a lock alone never proves descendants stopped.
decisions.why: The previous owner must lose dispatch authority while the new owner retains a resumable export.

decisions.decision: Return a private version-1 transfer receipt containing transfer UUID, canonical request SHA-256, source inventory digest, old-owner closure entries, source audit seal SHA-256 list, destination owner/audit and a sorted per-runtime effective-mapping array. Each mapping binds provider, SHA-256 of observed native session ID, relative runtime path, immutable creation-receipt SHA-256, completion SHA-256, export-manifest SHA-256, destination effective owner/audit and transfer UUID. The wire_contract section is normative for all schemas, projections, sorting, exact byte encoding and hash exclusions; both sides use its shared core implementation. The controller acknowledges only after checking this receipt against its immutable pending request and current ledger authority. Completion is not owner-message applied, review passed, model readiness, ship or deployment. Caller must persist pending handoff before external I/O, recheck its current lease before acknowledgement and reject partial receipts for native dispatch.
decisions.why: The core runtime transfer cannot substitute for the workflow state machine.

decisions.decision: Make scope-exit retirement carry the owner/audit observed at native launch. NativeSession retirement entries hold path plus expected effective owner/audit, not only a path. At retirement, reacquire StateLock, resolve current effective ownership and mark only if it still equals that expected authority. A delayed old controller Drop cannot retire a runtime transferred to a newer owner. Fresh independent reviewers still retire their own unmigrated runtimes; retained builder scopes remain retained under #1746. Launch::observe_session must apply the same captured-authority fence under StateLock before adding an alias. Refuse publication when the captured effective owner/audit has changed, is retired or belongs to a pending transfer. A delayed response from the source controller cannot add aliases to the destination runtime. Ordinary scope-exit retirement must also check durable pending owner/runtime claims under StateLock. If claimed, leave all runtime bytes and retirement markers unchanged and return retained-for-pending-handoff; do not abort, release claims/reservations, append to a sealed source audit or repeatedly retry from Drop. Only the existing explicitly authorized fenced-retirement entry point may invoke D10. The pending handoff owns retention/replay; after authorized abortion, the workflow reconciler settles affected registered source owners under existing verified retirement/recovery authority. A skipped Drop does not grant it retirement authority.
decisions.why: Kernel worker quiescence does not prove an old controller has dropped every Rust Arc; unconditional path-only retirement would bypass handoff fencing.

decisions.decision: Preparing a transfer durably claims every source/destination owner, audit log/anchor and runtime path. Claims are exclusive across pending transfers, with identity normalized under the canonical state root and actual protected audit namespaces. Owner claim identity is workflow_id plus lease_generation, independently of audit filename. Reusing the identical prepared transfer reuses its claims; an overlapping different transfer defers native-transfer-lock-busy before sealing any audit. Independent disjoint workflows can proceed. New native preparation and late alias publication check pending authority claims and defer without a model admission. Release claims atomically with completed or aborted state. Claims survive crashes; a StateLock alone is not a durable reservation. Persist the immutable association from each declared audit path to its canonical actual log and anchor. Claim actual log files as well as anchors, so alternate path aliases or anchor names cannot bypass endpoint exclusion. Identical-request replay rejects changed associations, even when the set of actual paths is unchanged. At native preparation capture the protected logger canonical actual-log path in Launch. Delayed observe_session checks this captured actual-log claim under StateLock as well as captured owner/runtime/raw audit authority. Do not re-resolve the declared path after a response: an alias may have rebound while the original protected logger still names the claimed namespace.
decisions.why: One transaction prevents partial ownership mappings, but partial audit sealing across a crash can still strand another transfer unless both endpoints are reserved. Admission and late response publication occur at different times; both must consume the same immutable namespace identity.

decisions.decision: Existing controller-authorized fenced retirement may supersede a pending transfer. Under StateLock, atomically mark every prepared transfer intersecting the retired owner/audit aborted, record native-transfer-authority-conflict, release its claims/growth reservation and persist the requested owner closure in the same native SQLite transaction. Then perform existing per-session retirement only where resolved effective owner equals that requested owner. Abortion does not migrate mappings, close additional source owners, fabricate a completed receipt, erase history or unseal an audit. Other registrations are settled only after an authorized terminal or independently verified per-namespace recovery producer has created their retirement intent. The existing reconciler consumes intents; it does not invent that authority. Remaining source namespaces without such intent stay retained with native-transfer-authority-conflict. Their named explicit recovery is authenticated owner cancellation through T/D, which creates terminal retirement intents for every registered owner, or independently verified per-namespace audit recovery. Public consumer enablement remains blocked until those paths and delivery of the hold are implemented. Aborted UUID replay returns a provenance hold and cannot restart or change destination. Completed historical transfers remain immutable; subsequent retirement changes only current authority eligibility. Corrupt pending state refuses retirement and requires explicit verified reconciliation.
decisions.why: Cancellation or verified audit recovery must retire its exact owned state while preventing stale prepared handoff from reviving it. It cannot wait forever on a transfer whose active workflow lease is gone.

decisions.decision: Expose ownership::transfer through the exact AUGMENTAGENT_NATIVE_VM_POLICY selection used by Launch; no public arbitrary-root override. The controller supplies TransferObservation {revision,sha256,certain} derived from its latest immutable observation history and a typed lease callback returning NotCurrent or Unavailable. Invalid request/observation refuses before state/audit mutation; uncertain observation is a conversation-uncertain hold. NotCurrent is an authority-conflict hold; inability to inspect the lease is persist-retry, never authority. Return typed Completed/Deferred/Held/Unknown and provide an explicit public_status projection that excludes private receipt paths and native IDs. Do not serialize the whole outcome. Typed reason values, rather than exception-message parsing, cross internal boundaries. Active in-process audit writers and kernel-populated resources defer lock-busy; interrupted writer receipts, changed host/resource identity and broken audit continuity remain provenance holds. After an orchestration error, re-read the exact UUID under StateLock: a verified completed receipt wins even after response failure, abortion holds authority-conflict, known absent/prepared state permits only the bounded classified outcome, and unreadable or uncertain durable state returns Unknown with that same UUID. Unknown never authorizes a new transfer or dispatch. The workflow caller still persists/reconciles the original request and rechecks its lease before settlement/dispatch.
decisions.why: An anyhow error cannot tell the scheduler whether to wait, require verified recovery, or reconcile a potentially committed transfer. Reconstructing authority from error text or starting a fresh UUID after uncertain persistence could strand sealed exports or repeat migration.

decisions.decision: A pending workflow handoff must persist a private versioned original authority-store binding before calling transfer: original policy-byte SHA-256, canonical native state root, stable storage epoch, root identity and native ledger file identity. Productive transfer must compare that stored binding with the current selected native policy/store before interpreting UUID absence or preparing anything. A mismatch is an authority-conflict hold, never a lookup in the replacement store or a fresh UUID. Historical receipt reconciliation may inspect only the originally bound store under current workflow authorization, without native dispatch, creating a replacement database or recapturing a new binding. Missing, replaced or unreadable original authority returns exact-UUID Unknown and preserves the pending workflow request. Store identity must survive restart and be checked by native launch/resume/retirement as well as transfer; missing/replaced authority cannot be silently initialized over saved runtimes. Establishing a new storage epoch requires explicit fresh provisioning or verified migration of an existing valid legacy ledger, not inference from a missing database or an empty directory. Bind and validate that identity before the first productive dispatch and retain it through normal rollout. Original-store historical lookup is distinct from productive ownership transfer, including when newer observations become uncertain.
decisions.why: Outcome fingerprints are retry hints, not a durable grant to reinterpret a request in a different ledger. A root/policy switch or missing database could otherwise turn a committed or prepared UUID into apparent absence and permit lost-history replay. The present API does not yet implement this binding and remains a public-enable blocker.

failure_and_replay: Before prepare: validation/busy/unknown failures change no effective owner or retired-owner authority. Caller exposes a bounded reason and retries only on a relevant change or persisted S backoff.
After prepare but before sealing: replay revalidates immutable inventory and uses the same transfer request. It cannot invent or substitute an observed session.
After a source audit seal but before its proof is stored: replay obtains the identical immutable proof from the anchor. A sealed source is never unsealed; pending handoff remains visible.

After seal proofs but before the native SQLite commit: pending replay performs the one transaction. If commit succeeded but its response was lost, the same ID returns the completed receipt without replaying old mappings. A later transfer or retirement cannot be undone by that replay.

Missing/corrupt prepared records, changed source metadata and incompatible authority remain explicit held/unknown outcomes. Preserve all runtime/audit bytes; no ownership guessing or model dispatch. Caller integration must provide a named reconciler or explicit operator recovery before public consumer enablement.

Concurrent/restarted requests consult durable endpoint claims before preparing or sealing. Fenced retirement atomically aborts an overlapping prepared transfer; lost-response replay observes aborted state and cannot resurrect authority. Completed replay remains historical after later retirement.
build_order_with_testable_exits: 1. Real filesystem red tests: old owner cannot safely resume under a distinct new audit; current retirement destroys that path. Add healthy anchored-audit seal tests, including busy/forged resource identity, pending writer, corruption and immutable seal replay.

2. Implement transfer validation, locks and durable ledger. Test Codex and Claude fixtures with exact aliases and completed exports. Verify no metadata writes on invalid/unknown inventory or live session lock. Include certain -> uncertain -> refusal, multiple retained sessions for one provider and invalid/overlong observed native IDs.

3. Add subprocess crash injection after prepare, each audit seal and native ledger commit before response. Replay must preserve creation receipts, exports and aliases byte-for-byte and never downgrade a later transfer. Race two controllers and destination/source retirement with transfer. Prove a delayed old scope Drop cannot mark a transferred session retired. Crash after only one source seal, then attempt overlap: defer before any other source/destination audit changes. A disjoint transfer must advance. Race fenced retirement against prepared/committed transfers; aborted replay cannot migrate or revive ownership. A delayed Launch::observe_session must not publish a source alias after handoff. Exercise delayed Drop during prepared state, after only one source seal, after completed state and after authorized abortion; it never independently aborts or leaks authority, and pending/caller reconciliation owns retained state.

4. Run affected native/audit suites through scripts/cargo-managed.sh and required hosted CI. No paid provider dispatch in these core fixtures. Attach tested source hashes as a list of path/sha256 records and preserve failed artifacts.

5. Only after this core contract passes: implement the caller protocol in WorkflowGuard, ownership promotion, owner-turn completion/pause preservation and public gateway/worker consumer. Then perform real guarded Codex/Claude continuation and Discord live acceptance. Core merge alone never closes D or E.
non_goals: No host shell fallback, new provider subscription, refresh grant expansion, lowered resource floor, provider route changes, owner pause removal, review/CI bypass or external message sending.
No import or relabel of uncertain legacy native conversations. Keep them held for explicit existing reconciliation or a separately verified fresh-conversation handoff.
No changes to merge-only accounting or shipping allowance authority.

open_threads.question: Before caller coding/enablement, implement an immutable observation table keyed by workflow/provider/session/observation sequence retaining certainty, binding, source owner/audit and observation time. Select the latest observation per retained runtime regardless of certainty, then refuse if that latest observation is uncertain; never filter uncertainty away before selecting. Only an explicit verified reconciliation may establish a subsequent certain observation. Read this immutable history, not only workflow_builder_conversation (latest per provider), and exclude uncertain/missing provenance. Preserve the existing session-owner uniqueness fence. The request uses the shared wire_contract and complete core-scanned runtime inventory. Implement durable preparation/promotion plus a named handoff reconciler through S persistence; all are public-enable blockers. Derive source_owners from every target-workflow native-owner registration with no retired_at and no retirement intent, including registrations with no runtime; reconcile pending retirement intents first. The observation history supplies eligible conversation mappings, not the complete owner-registration set. Wire existing authorized terminal/audit-recovery retirement intents to D10; elapsed time grants neither abortion nor retirement. Implement caller_registration_contract, including destination exclusion, receipt-backed transferred disposition, lost-response and cleanup-only terminal settlement. Remaining aborted peer namespaces without independently authorized intent are explicitly held for the named T/D cancel or verified namespace-recovery path; the intent consumer cannot manufacture authority. Apply observation_contract and original_store_binding_contract before defining the durable pending schema. open_threads.question: Specify and implement authenticated corrupt-prepared-state recovery. Existing cancellation/namespace intent consumers correctly refuse corrupt prepared rows; feeding the same consumer another intent is not a recovery protocol. Define trusted evidence, global versus workflow scope, permanent fencing/decommission or exact-authority reconstruction, anti-rollback behavior, atomic claim/reservation/closure effects and current-workflow settlement. No data repair, claim release, fabricated completion, old-policy recapture or database deletion may be inferred from a timeout or malformed row. Supported deployment snapshots can supply evidence/rollback artifacts but never by themselves recreate current ownership authority.

ledger_retention.authority_owner: Native runtime storage manager; this amendment adds no ledger garbage collector.
ledger_retention.retention: Transfer requests, completed receipts, source audit seal bindings, chain links and owner-closure tombstones are append-only and retained indefinitely, including after runtime directory reclamation. Runtime pruning never removes this database or its authority records.
ledger_retention.capacity: Before preparing a new transfer, enforce a 128 MiB native ledger budget and the existing policy state budget. Account for live SQLite/WAL bytes plus twice the encoded request/immutable-claim/proof/receipt upper bound and 1 MiB allocation margin. Refuse native-transfer-history-capacity when the reservation will not fit; do not lower resource floors, delete authority history or overwrite a pending request. Existing receipt replay remains read-only apart from SQLite recovery and does not allocate new transfer history. A commit or fsync failure after sealing remains a visible pending handoff for safe replay after supported capacity restoration. Persist reserved_bytes in every prepared transfer. Subsequent transfer admission counts the full reservations of all unresolved transfers in addition to actual DB/WAL bytes; conservatively retain each full reservation while its state is prepared. Release the reservation atomically with either completed or aborted terminal state, retaining its historical accounting. A crash preserves it. Before normal native runtime allocation, native preparation also deducts outstanding transfer growth from both the policy state budget and available filesystem capacity while preserving its existing 1 GiB free-space guard. Pending replay uses its existing reservation and is not admitted as a new transfer; never double-reserve it. Bound stored seal references to 1 MiB and completed receipt to 256 KiB; prepare computes its exact request and immutable-claim lengths plus those maxima before reservation. Larger proof material stays in its protected source anchor, with path/hash references in the ledger. Before preparing claims or sealing any audit, build the exact encoded receipt and seal-reference size projection using fixed-length placeholder hashes. If that immutable output cannot fit the 256 KiB receipt or 1 MiB reference bound, or one request/claim reservation cannot fit an otherwise empty 128 MiB ledger, return Held(native-transfer-invalid-request) with no prepared record, claims, closure or audit changes. More physical capacity cannot repair an inherently oversized immutable request; it needs verified replanning or the existing explicit cancellation/recovery path. Actual accumulated-history or physical-state exhaustion retains the capacity outcome.
ledger_retention.future_trigger: Any future ledger compaction requires a separate reviewed migration that preserves permanent fencing tombstones, every live runtime ownership chain and completed-receipt replay authority. It is outside this amendment; no current reader may assume such compaction.

wire_contract.shared_implementation: Expose one native-core canonical_bytes/request_digest/inventory_digest/verify_receipt implementation and typed version-1 request/receipt structures to the workflow caller. Caller and core must use it; do not implement independent serializers.
wire_contract.canonical_bytes: Recursively sort object keys by UTF-8 bytes; compact JSON, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8 output, no Unicode normalization, no floats. Emit non-ASCII characters literally; escape quote and backslash, use \b/\t/\n/\f/\r for those five controls and lowercase \u00xx for other U+0000..U+001F. Never escape slash or printable non-ASCII characters. Include byte-level vectors with non-ASCII, slash, backslash, quotes and controls.
request_fields: source_owners:array of {owner:{workflow_id,lease_generation},audit_path}, sorted by generation then audit_path bytes
inventory:array of runtime rows sorted by provider then runtime_relative_path bytes
inventory_row_fields: runtime_relative_path:provider/session-* relative to canonical native state root
export_manifest_sha256:hash of canonical derived export manifest
wire_contract.source_inventory_digest: SHA-256 of canonical_bytes({version:1,inventory:request.inventory}); include every row field exactly as declared. The canonical request hash covers the complete request with no omitted field.
wire_contract.export_manifest: Derived only; do not create a file inside the export. Object {version:1,entries:[...]}. Include every directory below the referenced generation, including empty directories, as {kind:"directory",path}; include each regular file as {kind:"file",path,bytes,sha256}. Exclude the generation root itself. Paths are UTF-8 POSIX relative paths with no empty, dot, parent or absolute component; preserve literal backslashes as filename characters. Reject invalid UTF-8, duplicate paths, symlinks and non-regular files. Sort entries by raw UTF-8 path bytes. File hashes cover original content bytes. D2 file/byte bounds and privacy checks apply. The existing producer limit of 2048 directories also applies; validate it without truncation. Every export generation root must be a same-UID directory with no group/other permission bits. Descendant directories must be same-UID, nonsymlink directories; legacy descendant mode bits are accepted only beneath that verified private root, which prevents other users from traversing the export. Regular files remain owner-private and single-link; all metadata stability checks remain mandatory. New producer exports create every directory component with mode 0700, independent of service umask. Never chmod or rewrite saved exports to make them eligible.
receipt_fields: source_seals:array of {audit_path,seal_sha256}, sorted by audit_path bytes

mappings:array of {provider,native_session_sha256,runtime_relative_path,creation_receipt_sha256,completion_sha256,export_manifest_sha256,effective_owner,effective_audit_path,transfer_id}, ordered as request.inventory and using destination authority
receipt_sha256:SHA-256 of canonical receipt object omitting only this field
wire_contract.verification: Reject unknown fields or versions, duplicate rows/source owners, incomplete source/session coverage, changed digest or destination. Source seal hash covers the canonical immutable proof returned by the anchor. Completed replay returns the stored receipt; current-authority verification is separate and may report superseded/retired while leaving that historical receipt intact.

outcome_contract.shape: Typed core result: Completed(receipt), Deferred(reason,fingerprint), Held(reason,fingerprint), Unknown(reason,transfer_id). No raw exception text is a public reason.
outcome_contract.projection: Capacity maps to S CapacityHold; dependency maps to S DependencyHold. Both are unpaid observations eligible next five-minute reconciliation cycle, subject to changed authoritative dependencies and capacity. Provenance holds require named explicit verified reconciliation/operator recovery; time alone never clears them. Transient I/O failure uses S persisted 5/10/20/40/60-minute backoff, capped at 60; ENOSPC maps to capacity instead. Unknown maps to reconciliation-only for the exact transfer UUID; no fresh native dispatch or new transfer. Success adds no ship/debit. The current command queue fixed five-minute scheduling is not the S failure backoff implementation. Aborted replay returns Held(native-transfer-authority-conflict), never Completed. Pending endpoint conflict returns Deferred(native-transfer-lock-busy). Fenced retirement remains the existing controller authorization boundary; abortion grants no new retirement authority.
outcome_contract.fingerprints: Bind reason plus request digest, native policy hash/state-root identity, observed conversation revision and alias/completion hashes; capacity adds current reservation/capacity class, transient failure adds fixed I/O category. Never include credentials, raw private paths or owner message text in public projection. The caller owns S persistence and the named handoff reconciler, both required before public enablement.
outcome_contract.controller_interface: TransferObservation carries revision >=1, a lowercase64 SHA-256 of immutable observation evidence, and certainty. Caller owns persisted 5/10/20/40/60 backoff and next-five-minute dependency/capacity reconciliation; this core API does not implement the scheduler.

caller_registration_contract.preparation: Claim a new reconciliation/preparation workflow lease without calling the existing WorkflowGuard constructor that registers the destination and appends workflow_claimed to the current source audit. Reconcile an existing pending native handoff before creating another. Select all eligible source registrations with generation strictly less than destination generation; explicitly exclude destination/current generation. Reconcile retirement intents first. Create the destination in a distinct audit namespace; register/promote its native authority only after core receipt settlement.
caller_registration_contract.settlement: Add immutable workflow-native handoff settlement records keyed by workflow/source generation/audit, binding transfer UUID, verified core receipt digest and destination owner/audit. In one workflow transaction validate the current reconciliation lease and immutable pending request, record every source as transferred in this separate disposition index, register the exact destination from the receipt and acknowledge the pending handoff. Do not repurpose terminal retirement flags or fabricate a retirement intent to represent transfer. Source selection excludes registrations with a verified transferred disposition as well as retired/retirement-intent rows. Duplicate settlement of the same receipt is idempotent; incompatible receipt or source association rejects.
caller_registration_contract.lost_response: A newer reconciliation lease may settle an older completed native request through the same receipt-backed metadata transaction, without reviving the old owner turn or granting native dispatch. If its generation differs from the settled destination, prepare a fresh handoff into the current generation before owner-turn promotion. A terminal workflow instead uses an explicit cleanup-only settlement API that revalidates its exact current terminal checkpoint identity, acknowledges only the stored pending request/verified historical receipt, and creates terminal retirement intent for the registered destination. It grants no productive lease, owner-message completion or dispatch.
caller_registration_contract.aborted_peers: For terminal cancellation, the existing terminal transition creates retirement intent for all registered owners and settlement adds any previously unregistered receipt-backed destination for cleanup. For nonterminal per-namespace recovery, only that independently verified namespace receives intent. Other sealed source namespaces after abortion stay explicitly held; the reconciler never assumes abortion itself authorizes their retirement. Authenticated whole-workflow cancel or independently verified per-namespace recovery is required. These named recovery and reporting paths are O2/O3 enablement blockers.

original_store_binding_contract.pending_record: Persist canonical request, its SHA-256, complete original private store binding and original observation projection together in the same workflow pending-handoff transaction. original_store_binding_contract.policy_change: Preserve the old store and request. original_store_binding_contract.bootstrap_and_loss: Establish a durable storage epoch through supported explicit fresh provisioning or verified existing-ledger migration. Bind root and database identities; a previously established ledger that disappears or is replaced is unknown authority, never an invitation to create empty state. Fresh bootstrap/crash protocol and policy-change historical-lookup behavior tests are implementation prerequisites.

observation_contract.status: Normative producer/evidence requirements; workflow/native launch-journal integration pending.
observation_contract.history_key: Append-only rows keyed by workflow, provider, runtime_relative_path and monotonic observation_sequence. Native session ID is nullable until actually observed; do not omit a launched runtime merely because its ID is unknown. Keep the existing cross-workflow session-owner uniqueness fence for known IDs. Select latest row per retained runtime regardless of certainty. This refines O2 prior provider/session wording so an unknown initial ID cannot disappear from history.
row_projection: launch_sha256:controller captured exact submitted native launch, or null when not established
protected_observation_reference:source audit namespace/sequence/digest, or null for explicitly missing evidence
observation_contract.normal_producer: Only the fenced workflow controller observing the real native bridge completion may append a normal certain observation. It binds the launch intent captured before submission, observed provider ID, owned runtime and complete/export/alias bytes. Failure, missing ID, missing durable evidence or interrupted submission appends uncertainty. Normal writes cannot overwrite an unresolved uncertain row with certain merely because the same ID reappears.
observation_contract.certainty_restoration: Only a named verified-reconciliation operation under a current reconciliation lease can append certainty after uncertainty. Its proof must identify the exact uncertain sequence and exact submitted launch; verify same workflow/provider/native ID/runtime and creation/effective authority; verify protected controller observation and correlated kernel-quiescent resource evidence; and verify successful nondiagnostic completion for that same launch plus unchanged original alias/export bindings. Completion from an older launch, a healthy login/PID, time, operator prose or a bare boolean is insufficient. Missing historical launch/controller proof stays held; it is never synthesized or imported from provider text. Independently authorized terminal/namespace retirement can end retention but does not relabel that conversation certain.
observation_contract.aggregate: The fenced workflow store creates or reuses an immutable positive-sequence observation snapshot for the exact workflow binding, complete eligible-source-registration digest and complete selected latest-row projections. Identical authoritative inputs reuse the same snapshot and sequence; retries never mint a new sequence merely because time or a process changed. TransferObservation.revision is this persisted snapshot sequence, not max(runtime row sequence). sha256 is SHA-256 of canonical_bytes({version:1,workflow_id,revision,workflow_binding,source_registration_sha256,observations:[complete row projections sorted by provider/runtime_relative_path UTF-8 bytes]}). All selected row sequences must precede the snapshot sequence. certain is true only when every required latest row has verified certainty and the controller scan accounts for every retained runtime. Separate registration-derived source_owners still includes owners with zero runtimes.
observation_contract.implementation_gate: Persist launch/controller proof references and immutable history before enabling any productive consumer. Add exact-launch versus older-completion, missing-ID, certain-to-uncertain refusal, insufficient-recovery-proof and verified append-only restoration tests. No legacy backfill may invent missing proof.
reconciliation_proof_projection: resource_proofs:complete controller-read run_resources::verify_quiescent return objects sorted by canonical identity bytes
proof_sha256:SHA-256 canonical complete proof omitting only this field
observation_contract.proof_producer: The native storage verifier reads exact runtime/launch/completion/alias/export metadata under StateLock then session lock and reads the protected source audit under its anchor gate; it verifies controller launch/ID observations and resource correlation as in D3. It returns the complete strict proof projection to the current workflow reconciliation lease for an append-only observation transaction. This operation cannot seal an audit, transfer ownership, write a retirement marker or dispatch a provider. Historical source evidence must already exist; missing launch/ID provenance refuses. The workflow transaction rechecks lease, binding, exact uncertain predecessor and proof digest before appending; its commit is the only producer of restored workflow certainty.
observation_contract.empty_inventory: An empty inventory uses the same persisted positive snapshot sequence and canonical aggregate with observations:[]. Certainty is true only after the bound native-store scan verifies there are no eligible non-retired runtimes and the complete registration-derived source set is supplied. Missing/unreadable scan evidence is a hold, never an empty inventory. The core independently rescans under StateLock at transfer, so a runtime appearing after snapshot capture refuses rather than disappearing from the request. A zero-runtime source owner still appears in source_owners and receives normal closure/seal handling.
